first.rationale: Onboarding completion is currently declining and two inherited records indicate that reducing onboarding and signup friction improves early adoption. This is the most direct reversible response with a plausible path to sustainable qualified revenue, while aggressive pricing may win acquisition but has material margin and downstream-value risk. Verify the onboarding evidence and the pricing result because both are highly consequential alternatives; retain uncertainty about whether activation and completion declines share the same cause.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. It directly addresses the 4% decline in onboarding completion and has verified evidence of +13% completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and +3% 30-day retention—an aligned path to sustainable qualified revenue. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified short-term qualified-revenue lift came with a 12% retention decline before first renewal. The experiment should measure qualified activation, time-to-value, and early retention alongside completion, since the current activation decline may have additional causes.
